answer: Use `show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency>`. The ocm-channel object lists the detected carriers within the configured OXcon(s), and is show-only (Operational Mode, Candidate Configuration Mode). Fields: name (String length 0..64), lower-frequency and upper-frequency (uint32) which are the lower/upper frequency of the corresponding spectrum power (OPM-pwr point), opm-pwr (Optical Parameter Monitor power in dBm, decimal64 range -99.00..99.00, default -99), and connected (true/false, default false), which yields 'true' if the channel is configured, that is, involved in an oxcon. Example: `show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency> opm-pwr connected`.

Yes. On ocm-mp the attribute ocm-enable, which enables regular power monitoring, takes disabled or enabled and defaults to enabled. Change it with `set ocm-mp-<name> ocm-enable disabled`. The full set command is `set ocm-mp-<name> [label] [admin-state] [ocm-enable]`; admin-state takes lock, unlock or maintenance with default unlock. Read-only companions: monitoring-state, which the system reports as enabled when an OMS reference exists (default enabled); monitored-port, the port being monitored, default not-applicable, which can differ from supporting-port for a non-integrated OCM; and ad-direction, the reference to the AD (coupler/splitter) DWDM port, which for ocm-mp is only ingress. ocm-mp is managed-by system.

The ocm-ptp facility is available for WS04S cards within a CD-AD ADG and provides dedicated OCM monitoring. It is not enabled out of the box: ocm-enable (enabled/disabled) defaults to disabled, so turn it on with `set ocm-ptp-1-1.2-ocm1-in ocm-enable enabled`. The set command also takes label and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock). Show-only attributes include ad-direction (egress or ingress, default ingress), last-measurement (last OCM scan date-and-time, or never, default never), adg-number (uint8 range 0..110, default 0) and monitoring-state (default disabled; the system reports enabled when complete connectivity at the AD is established and OCM measurement is possible).

On the oms facility, grid-mode defaults to flexible, which lets you create and delete MCs of different widths. The alternatives are fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif (R6.0.1 and later), fixed-50G-7100 (50GHz, 88 channels, set automatically when osc-compatibility is osc-7100, R7.0 and later) and fixed-150G-40ch. Default lower-frequency is 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 (standardC-band). monitoring-mode selects the monitoring/equalization behaviour: not-monitored (non-intrusive monitoring, no OCM/DGE required), intrusive (TTP), non-intrusive (CTP, operates with OCM such as DGE), dge-fixed-attenuation (fixed attenuation due to a connected interstage device), ila-with-equalization (operate with DGE and OCM) and integrated-equalization (integrated DGE). Default is intrusive for all node types except ILA, not-monitored for node-type ILA and integrated-equalization for hyperscale ILA nodes. It is only exposed for an OMS of a port that belongs to a degree, or on an ILA node.

`set ops-<name>` accepts label, admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), input-psd-profile, role and port-expansion. input-psd-profile is the nominal expected tributary channel power density in dBm/12.5GHz, decimal64 range -30..-6, default -6. role can be tributary (single add/drop to a local or remote transponder), multi-carrier (multiple carriers on the underlying filter port), general-purpose (the default, used for express cross-connection to another filter), ase-input (only available on specific RD ports in SLTE l0-mode-op) or active-multi-carrier (multiple carriers with active port control). supported-roles is read-only and exposes which roles the card, and sometimes the card-mode, permits. port-expansion is no (default) or y-cable. Example: `set ops-1-6-ad1 role tributary`.

On optical-carrier, frequency is the center frequency the carrier is tuned to, 0 meaning not configured; the generic range is 0 | 191275000..196125000 MHz but the real range and step depend on module and pluggable, for example CHM7 and CHM7X 190625000-196725000 MHz (step 50 MHz), CHM6 191333000-196117000 MHz (step 50 MHz), CHM2TX 191292500-196137500 MHz (step 1 MHz), TOM-400G-C-DWDM 191275000-196125000 MHz. tx-power is the transmit power into the fiber, overall range -55.0..55.00 dBm, adjustable in steps of 0.5 dBm, with per-module limits such as CHM2TX -6 to 0 (default 0), CHM7/CHM7X -10 to 0 (default -2) and UTM2 -15 to 0 (default -6.0); on TOM-100GFI-C-DWDM and the 10GMR SFP+ pluggables it is not configurable. For a slight trim use frequency-offset, int16 range -6000..6000 MHz, default 0: once set the frequency changes slowly over 1-10 s without affecting service.

Yes. `set optical-carrier-<name> propagate-shutdown enabled`. When propagate-shutdown is set, the transmit laser is shut down if the whole service of that direction has signal failure; the function is mainly used at a regeneration node to propagate signal failure as LOS. Values are enabled and disabled, default disabled. Pair it with propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer, the hold off time of propagate shutdown, range 0..2000 milliseconds, default 0. Restriction: neither propagate-shutdown nor propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer is configurable on the SPN2 or SPN2C card.

Very little. `set optical-channel-<name>` accepts only label (String length 0..256) and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), for example `set optical-channel-channel1 admin-state unlock`. Everything else is read-only through `show optical-channel-<name>`: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID (String length 1..64), oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state, and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user-created facilities can be user deleted). Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Read laser-state on the optical-ptp: `show optical-ptp-<name> laser-state`. It shows the emitting pump (for example booster) laser state as enabled or disabled, default disabled, and is only of relevance for DWDM line ports; on RD amplifiers it refers to the source (Tx) pump, on Raman modules to the pump laser. Yes, you can declare fixed pad on the receive side: fix-rx-attenuation is the fixed attenuator before port Rx, decimal64 with 2 fraction digits, range 0..30 dB, default 0, where 0 dB is equivalent to no fixed attenuator. Example: `set -f optical-ptp-1-6-dwdm fix-rx-attenuation 10`. There is a matching fix-tx-attenuation (fixed attenuator after port Tx, 0..30 dB, default 0) but it is only visible when ops.port-expansion=y-cable is configured. Measured levels are power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx (-99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99 dBm).

On optical-switch the Signal Fail thresholds are working-los-threshold and protection-los-threshold, both settable, both optical power in the range -55.0 to 0 dBm with default -23 dBm; received power below that declares the path failed. There is also facility-los-threshold, the threshold of the facility port below which loss of signal is declared, range -55 to 15 dBm, default -30.0 dBm. Signal Degrade switching uses working-switch-threshold and protection-switch-threshold (-55.0 to 0 dBm, default -18 dBm) and is only active when switch-threshold-enable is enabled (default disabled). Hysteresis is configurable: los-threshold-hysteresis (SF, default 3 dB) and switch-threshold-hysteresis (SD, default 2 dB), both decimal64 range 0.5 to 5.0 dB in steps of 0.1 dB, with 1 dB recommended for MCHP and OMSP deployments.

`set osc-<name>` accepts label, admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), l0-comm-interface-type (ipv4 or ipv6; ipv4 for standard OLS, ipv6 for SLTE and HSC OLS), osc-control (auto or manual, default auto; auto is supported from R6.0.1 and HSC OLS nodes support auto only), target-output-power (na, or -2.5..4.5 dBm, default na, defined at the DWDM Line port output), tx-power-adjustment (na for IR and LR OSC SFP types, or -6..6 dB, default 0, adjusting the automatically calculated Tx target in osc-control auto mode), voa-attenuation-target-rx (0..30 dB, default 10, used in manual control mode) and lof-soak-timer (short, effectively about 3 ms, default; or long, adding 18,400 OC-3 frames, about 2300 ms; only visible for the PBAx card and affecting OSC LOF alarm timing only). Read-only: monitoring-mode, oscc-support, osc-mode, osc-wavelength, voa-attenuation-actual-rx, power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx.

Use `show otdr-<name> otdr-state`. otdr-state indicates the current status of the OTDR and a status change triggers a change notification: not-available (default), idle, measuring (measurement ongoing), finished (measurement completed) or fail (measurement failed). Alongside it, otdr-measurement-time gives the time remaining in the running measurement (default 0), otdr-error carries the error message produced when the measurement ends with error, otdr-laser-state shows not-available/enabled/disabled, otdr-measurement-port shows the port being measured (0 means the card is not measuring any port), otdr-measurement-direction shows not-available/tx/rx (not-available means the scan is not running) and otdr-ongoing-measurement-profile shows none, short, medium, long or raman-precheck1/2/3. Per-port results such as otdr-last-measurement, otdr-last-measurement-file and otdr-fiber-break-distance are on otdr-ptp.

On otdr-ptp: otdr-range specifies the distance range in kilometers used to calculate the measurement repetition period, auto (default) or 0...300.0 km, and it is recommended to set the actual fiber length plus 10%; from R9.1, when the OTS can be traced from the fiber connection between the ILA/ROADM card and OTDR8OFP2, auto is derived from OTS fiber-length-tx/fiber-length-rx with 10% margin rounded up to the nearest 10 km. otdr-resolution is the data sampling resolution, auto or 0.4...100.0. otdr-pulse-width is auto or 10...20,000 ns and determines dynamic range together with the other parameters. otdr-measurement-speed is fast (about 10 s), medium (about 15 s), slow (about 1 minute), precision (about 3 to 5 minutes), high-precision (about 5 to 7 minutes) or auto (default). Also otdr-ior (auto, or 1.0...2.0), peak-power (auto, or 5...14.5) and launching-fiber-length (0...50 m, default 0; auto is not supported), which is deducted from the result.

On the ots facility. `set ots-<name>` takes fiber-type-tx and fiber-type-rx, chosen from AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor, both defaulting to SSMF (fiber-type-rx also accepts not-applicable, auto and not-configured). Lengths are fiber-length-tx and fiber-length-rx, auto by default or 0..500.0 km, required for tilt control when tilt-control-mode = auto and when Raman backward pumping is deployed. Loss is declared with span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive, decimal64 range 0..80 dB (receive also 99), default 0; changing span-loss-receive is traffic affecting. Non-fiber loss such as patch panels goes in external-attenuation-tx and external-attenuation-rx (0..30 dB, default 0). Also span-loss-aging-margin-rx (0.00..10.00 dB, default 1.0), fiber-spectral-attenuation-tilt-tx/rx (-1..1 dB/THz) and raman-coefficient-tx/rx (0..10 dB/THz/W). span-loss-reference (configured or measured, default measured) selects which value power control uses; derived values appear in fiber-length-derived-rx/tx and span-loss-derived-rx/tx.

The system generates it. The ots-diagnostics name is auto generated on line card provisioning, with the format 'ots-diagnostics-<chassis>-<slot>-<DWDM Line>', so you address it as, for example, `show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line` for an RD20TM DWDM line, or ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line1 and ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line2 for a C2ILASGH with two lines. Only two attributes are settable: nmoper-alarm-reporting (disabled by default; when enabled, a mismatch between expected-operator and rx-operator raises the NMOPER alarm, and disabling it clears the alarm immediately and stops the comparison) and expected-operator (up to 32 characters/bytes, empty by default). tx-operator is automatically defaulted by the system with the format '<ne-name>-<Dxx>', default <ne-name>-D00.

ots-r assumes SSMF. required-fiber-type-rx is the required fiber type on the DWDM Line with reference to the Rx fiber, default SSMF, selected from AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor; it is only of relevance if control-mode = auto and when there is no fiber-connection. The rest of the receive span is declared with fiber-length-rx (unspecified by default, or 0..500.0), span-loss-receive (default 99), external-attenuation-rx, delta-pointloss (not-applicable by default, or -1..3.5 dB, the fiber contribution to point loss to be fine tuned in the field, for example a bad splice at dwdm-line Rx) and target-power-setting (manual or auto, default auto), plus label, admin-state (default unlock) and alarm-report-control (default allowed). Read-only: configured-fiber-type-rx, configured-fiber-length-rx, span-loss-at-amplifier, power-actual-rx and connected-reference.

Yes, and yes. `set ots-r-auto-otdr-<name> automatic-otdr enabled|disabled` enables or disables the OTDR based automatic fiber check. The default is enabled for green field deployments and disabled for in-field SW upgrade. In addition, if the Raman card is associated with a base card equipped with an integrated OTDR the default is enabled, and if the NE has a Raman card that is not aggregated with the EDFA card the value is disabled. The setting persists over warm and cold restart and over SW upgrade. Disabling it while a test is running aborts the ongoing OTDR test and allows the amplifier blocked by the automatic OTDR to be activated; when enabled, tests are triggered at the next opportunity when the pre-conditions and triggering criteria are met. Progress is shown by auto-otdr-state (not-applicable, not-available, pass, in-progress, fail, aborted) and results by external-attenuation-rx-measured (0..55 dB) and total-reflectance-rx-measured (-99..99 dB). loss-calibration-by-otdr (none default, rx-only, tx-only, tx-rx) decides whether measured values feed Power Control.

Use `add oxcon-<name> source <value> destination <value>` with the two media channel end-points, for example `add oxcon-1-80-192262500__1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 source 'nmc-1-80-192262500' destination 'nmc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500'`. Optional on add: label, activation-mode, auto-delete, activation-request-fwd/bwd, direction (two-way default, or one-way), target-output-power-src and target-output-power-dst (decimal64 range -18.00..15.00 dBm; default 0 dBm, or -5 dBm when an Add/Drop OXcon is created between a Tributary NMC and an RD20TM/RD09SM NMC) and circuit-id. Whether it comes up on its own depends on activation-mode: automatic, the default in standard L0 mode, activates the service automatically on creation and deactivates it on deletion; manual (SLTE mode) and activate-on-create (HSC OLS mode) are driven manually through activation-request-fwd and activation-request-bwd (no-request, activate, deactivate), with activation-state-fwd/bwd reporting activated, partially-activated, faulted or deactivated.

profile-control applies only to RD20TM operating in card-mode = slte or slte-backhaul, and only in Operational Mode. Syntax: `profile-control [type=]<value> [entity=]<value> [direction=]<value> [[profile-data=]<value>]`. type is write-attenuation-profile, read-attenuation-profile, create-power-profile, read-power-profile or read-ocm-power; entity references the object (an OMS or an NMC); direction is tx or rx, and for power-profile only tx is supported. Example: `profile-control read-power-profile oms-1-8-dwdm-line tx`. For RD20TM in card-mode = slte the power profile and OCM power are defined at the output of the booster, before the EVOA, not at the DWDM line out port. The OMS attenuation string is '<StartFreq>,<SlotWidth>,<AttnValue1>,...,<AttnValueN>' with StartFreq in MHz, SlotWidth in GHz, attenuation values 0 to 25.50 and N = 776 for standardC-band at 6.25 GHz granularity; for NMC the values range -10 to 25.50 and N cannot exceed 32.

Not much. `set pump-<name>` accepts only label (String length 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance) and alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default Allowed). Everything else on the pump command is show-only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled), avail-state (in-service, out-of-service, normal, abnormal, low-power), managed-by (system or user, where only user created facilities can be user deleted) and pump-type. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Pump power levels are not on this command: use pump-power for target-pump-power, configured-pump-power and actual-pump-power.

Use `set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> target-pump-power <value>`, where pump-id is an integer identifying the number of the pump. target-pump-power is the Raman pump power required, in dBm, and applies when the control-mode is manual; permitted values are -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable (the default), with 0 used for the not-applicable case. If the card is RPBM, target-pump-power must be in the range 12 to 30 dBm. If the value is outside the operating range of the Raman sled, the alarm PUMP-Fail (STAT FAIL PSTAT) is raised. How high it may go is reported by max-target-pump-power, with min-target-pump-power for the lower bound; both are decimal64 with 2 fraction digits, range -99.00..99.00 dBm, or not-applicable. configured-pump-power shows the value programmed in hardware (derived automatically when control-mode is auto, otherwise from target-pump-power) and actual-pump-power the currently measured value (default -99).

Use `show raman-calibration-<name> calibration-state`, for example `show raman-calibration-1-8`. calibration-state displays the state of the automatic Raman gain calibration process: not-available (the default: calibration has not been triggered or no prior calibration has occurred), in-progress (currently running), up-to-date (completed successfully and current), out-dated (stale due to OTS OLOS, a change in delta pointloss and similar) or fail (ended with a failure). Supporting read-only fields: last-calibration-timestamp (date-and-time, or never, default never), gain-calibration-error (residual gain error after each iteration in dB, or not-available), calibrated-delta-pointloss (suggested delta-pointloss at the end of each iteration, -3..3.5 dB, or not-available), intermediate-results (string up to 1024), and additional-info, which carries troubleshooting information when calibration-state is fail or out-dated. The only settable attribute is label.

rsc is the Raman card Pilot Tone facility. `set rsc-<name>` takes label, admin-state (Unlock, Locked, Maintenance, Unknown; default Unlocked) and alarm-report-control (Allowed or Inhibited, default Allowed). It reports two Pilot Tone measurements: rsc-power-rx, the received Pilot Tone integrated power, and rsc-power-tx, the transmitted Pilot Tone integrated power. The remaining show fields are supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled or disabled, default enabled), avail-state and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user created facilities can be user deleted). Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Because the OMS underneath is not in a monitoring-mode that creates it. The spectrum facility is only instantiated by the system when the underlying server layer, OMS, has monitoring-mode configured either as non-intrusive or ila-with-equalization; the existence of this managed object depends on the OMS monitoring-mode. The object is only of relevance if the DGE2 is intended to be used in the NE. Set the OMS monitoring-mode accordingly and the spectrum object appears. On the object, dge-in-use reports true if the corresponding OMS monitoring-mode is ila-with-equalization (default false), and attenuation-setting is the unique attenuation value for the entire spectrum, range 0..30 dB, default 0 dB, editable when attenuation-control-mode = manual and control-mode = auto-max-pw.

Use spectrum-control, which is keyed by name, direction and center-frequency: `set spectrum-control-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> attenuation-target <value>` or target-output-power, for example `set spectrum-control-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/194943750 attenuation-target 1`. direction is ingress or egress, but only egress is currently supported (default egress). center-frequency is the band slice center frequency in MHz and is managed by the system. attenuation-target is the required attenuation for the spectra, range 0..30 dB, default 0, and is only possible to configure when a Dynamic Gain Equalizer, or equivalent, is in use (dge-in-use = 'true'). target-output-power is the intended target output power, not-specified (default) or -55..55 dBm. Read-only: attenuation-actual, only readable when a DGE is in use, and width, the detected width from spectrum-monitoring in MHz, which returns 0 if the configured center-frequency matches no spectrum or if no ILAx card or DGE is fiber-connected.
